Proud spirit or temper; their noble passions angered and roused.
Trojan; of the land around Troy, named after Dardanus, legendary founder of the Trojan line.
Name of one of the six gates of Troy.

Lacking skill or experience; inexpert, untrained.
Split apart; tear or break in two.
Speak disparagingly of; belittle or criticize.

Short form of Pandarus, Cressida's uncle and Troilus's go-between in the courtship.

Descent, family lineage; related by kinship.

Jackdaws: small, common crow-like birds, used contemptuously for ordinary or worthless people in contrast to noble eagles.

while not yet won (a man must plead); once won, he commands
Greek; belonging to the Greeks.
lofty, superior position; high rank above the others

Ill-fitted, unsuited to the matter; crude and disproportionate, like timber or stone not cut to shape.
Delight, gratification (the spleen being thought the seat of laughter); i.e. from laughing so hard.
two; the pair (of people just mentioned).
lofty, haughty; an exalted position he carries himself in arrogantly
mere map-making; armchair strategy done over maps rather than in actual fighting (said contemptuously)
Greek; belonging to the Greeks.

the person being praised
fame or glory won by deeds; renown

What little life and vigour remains in an old man.
Forbid; prevent (used in wishing something may not happen).
Split open, cleave (as wood is split by wedges).
Escape; come away from (a fight with) unharmed.
Achilles, leader of the Myrmidons, the fierce warrior people of Thessaly who followed him to Troy.
Of a she-wolf; an insult meaning son of a savage female dog, i.e. son of a bitch.
Belonging to Proserpina, queen of the underworld in Roman myth, wife of Pluto; Cerberus guarded her realm.
Title for a woman, used mockingly to insult a man as womanish or a scolding shrew.
Used as an insult: you barbarous, uncouth lout; brutishness in person.
Term of abuse: a dull, lumbering beast of burden, i.e. a stupid brute fit only for carrying loads.
Part of the Latin phrase pia mater: the membrane enclosing the brain, hence the brain itself.
Assure, promise (you); used to stress a statement: no, certainly not.
Voluntarily; of my own free will, as a volunteer rather than a hired or forced servant.
Voluntarily; willingly, by his own choice.
Blockheads; dull, stupid fellows (literally, heads like clods of earth).
Overconfidence; a sense of complete safety that leads to carelessness.
Scolded, rebuked; here, sent running after a reprimand.

An act of retaliation or reprisal (here, for the Greeks' earlier seizure of Hesione, Priam's sister).
Spoken words, voiced approval; here imagined as wind filling the sails.

Priam's royal palace in Troy (in this play, distinct from the city itself).
Passion or temper, thought of as seated in the blood.
Mad, frenzied; produced by a disordered mind.
unanimous agreement; collective approval given with one accord

Passions or impulses, as opposed to reason.

Corpse; dead body.

Fathered, begot (past tense of get).
Will, command; Pandarus means whose orders, but the servant takes it as enjoyment.

Greek; belonging to the Greeks.
Myself (royal or formal 'we' used by a single speaker); i.e. outshines even me.
Form of address to a male social inferior or servant, expressing command or familiarity; roughly 'you there, fellow'.

Having healing power; serving as a remedy or medicine.
Showy trinkets or toys; cheap, flashy novelties.
Drove; old past tense of drive, here meaning forced or compelled (Mars to take sides).

Speech, spoken words (as opposed to writing).

jester; the licensed buffoon kept for amusement (here Thersites)

great-souled; noble and lofty in spirit (a grand honorific title, used mockingly here)
Latin for 'and'; with cetera, meaning 'and so on', 'and the rest' (here cutting short a string of titles).

Utterance; 'given good words breath' means spoken good words aloud.

Greek warrior, son of Achilles (also called Pyrrhus); here probably used loosely for Achilles himself, the most famous Greek fighter.
